scope: Source lineage and original byte identities, not a claim of unchanged deployed tools or inherited test results.
port_changes: Python package-relative imports replace sibling-script imports.
An explicit data root (FIST_KB_ROOT, set by the public CLI) replaces a root inferred from the installed tool location; the binding root stays the KB folder's parent.

Tool identity is checked against the shipped Python package manifest instead of KnowledgeBase/tools/inventory.json; admin record-tools is removed and admin verify-tools also reports the package check.
The guest reader checks and executes the packaged engine bytes listed in the package manifest; no code in a KB folder is loaded or executed.
Command hints name the fist-kb CLI instead of kb.py.
Migration writes empty text, not the text None, for a null purpose or owner in the old core (Fist KB 0.3.x stored a null purpose).
Migration maps old origin types by generic words only; any other type becomes import, and the original origin is still logged verbatim.
Public commands isolate engine invocations in child Python processes run with -P; read and write requests travel on stdin.
Public writes, preparation, initialization and migration use an exclusive per-KB lock; reads do not create locks, and stale locks are never removed automatically.
Initialization creates correctly bound empty data through the engine's own init, without agent-role instructions or a Seed installer.
